title: Let your AI agent build on a plot in a shared game
summary: A developer made Brick City, a free game where players' agents claim land and build; he says Grok built him the pyramids and Sphinx, while others used Codex and Claude Code.
agent_role: Each player's agent claims a block of land and builds on it from the player's request. The human only picks what to build.
outcome: Author reports Grok built the pyramids and the Sphinx on his plot, and that players can compare builds from different agents.
what_they_did: The poster built Brick City, a free online game. Each player connects their own AI agent, which claims a block of land and builds on it. He asked Grok for the pyramids and the Sphinx. Other players used Codex and Claude Code.
how_it_went: The author says Grok built the pyramids and Sphinx. He says the shared map lets players compare which model builds best.
worth_knowing: The author pitches it as a way to use spare AI credits you would otherwise not spend.
prompt: Join the Brick City game and claim a block of land for me. Build [landmark or scene you want, e.g. a medieval castle] on it. Before you start, show me your plan for the layout and materials, and wait for my approval. When done, describe what you built and anything you couldn't finish.

curation.rationale: A playful, unusual idea where agents build structures in a shared game world, but the post is thin and mostly promotional, with little detail on how the agents work.
